task.title: Inspect a Topicmap Sign
task.shortdesc: Open the Topicmap of an edit proposal in the local Catalog, press on a Topic sign and on a Role edge, and reach the projected Topic, the TMDM object and the TMDM Role that they stand for.

prereq.p: A local review Catalog started with scripts/serve-ctm-page-authoring.lisp from a commit that has the Role edge gesture or a later one, serving a site root that holds the page ctm-and-tmdm-in-hyperdoc. A Catalog started from an older commit does not offer the gesture on a Role edge. The concepts are in Topicmap Signs and Represented Objects and TMDM Roles and Projected Edges; the Operations are in Topicmap Gesture Operations.

context.p: Each step names the view or the Operation that it uses. Nothing in this task writes to the wiki: preparing a proposal and looking at its Topicmap are reading.

step.cmd: Open the Item and prepare a proposal.
step.info: Open the Item E3 (registered-story-item) from the Work Breakdown page Author the CTM Plan Page. In its Edit view choose Prepare edit proposal. The pane to the right shows an item-edit-proposal. A completion shows the same Topicmap with more objects.

step.cmd: Open the Topicmap view of the proposal.
step.info: Choose the tab Topicmap. The native Topicmap draws the objects of the Item edit, each Association as a node of its own and one edge for each Role. The Point panel below the drawing names the Topic at the Point. The Point starts at the proposal.

step.cmd: Press the secondary button on the node proposes and wait.
step.info: Hold the secondary button on the sign of the Association node for about half a second. The radial menu appears with two entries: Inspect represented object to the left and Inspect Topicmap sign upward. Move in the direction of the entry and release. Releasing without a move chooses nothing and opens nothing. This is the Binding of the radial menu.

Press the secondary button, move to the left at once and release. This is the learned mark; it completes with the same Operation and opens the same object as the menu, which you can check by the identical object address in the pane title.

Upward opens the projected Topic, an item-edit-topic whose Provenance view says how HyperDoc knows the Association and why. To the left opens the TMDM Association it represents. The two are different objects (see the concept topic).
step.stepresult: The Point and the History are as they were: a secondary press is a reading Operation.

step.info: Press the secondary button on the edge between proposes and the-proposed-action. The edge has a transparent hit line about 14 pixels wide, below the Topic signs. The menu offers only Inspect represented object; there is no Relation Contract. Choosing it, by the menu or by a mark to the left, opens the TMDM Role.

step.cmd: Navigate from the Role to its objects.
step.info: In the pane of the Role choose the tab Slots. The slots parent, type and player open the TMDM Association, the Role type and the player.

step.cmd: Return to the projection and its provenance.
step.info: In the Topicmap choose a Topic with a primary click: the Point moves there and its panel shows the provenance and the Roles. The Provenance view of a projected Topic ends in a link back to the Topicmap. The History is shown by Open the Workspace as a pane.

step.cmd: Compare PRIMARY in the native Topicmap and in TALA.
step.info: In the native Topicmap a primary click on a Topic sign moves the Point and records the History; a primary click on a Role edge does nothing. Choose Lay out with TALA and then the tab TALA (interactive): there a primary click on a Topic or an edge opens its object in a pane and no Point exists. A secondary press offers the same Operations on the Topic groups, and on a Role edge the single Operation Inspect represented object.

result.p: Every object named in the steps is an object of the running image: the pane titles carry its class and address, and two panes of one object show one address.

postreq.p: What this task cannot show: the automated browser tests dispatch synthetic pointer events (isTrusted is false). They exercise the element, the Gesture transport, the reducer and the Operations, and prove nothing about a physical mouse or trackpad, for example whether a trackpad delivers a secondary press, a move and a release as one sequence. Try the steps with a mouse first and with the trackpad second; if the mouse works and the trackpad does not, the input device is the cause, not the Operations.
